Subject: Private offer for Azure reserved capacity — discount path and channel carveout

Hi Naomi,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. Clearwater is preparing a private offer request for Azure-reserved capacity across EMEA (pilot) with phased expansion to APAC and NA in year two. Key asks from our side: 

- A 35–45% off list discount corridor for year one (we're targeting ~40% blended) tied to a 12–18 month committed spend.
- A clear, auditable channel rebate to our reseller network (we use two distributors in EMEA). We need the rebate to be reflected in the private offer routing or through a distributor credit path so our partners don't get double-taxed.
- Ability to smooth volume month-to-month (we anticipate seasonality) without losing corridor eligibility.
- Documentation for procurement: a draft PO and any evidence for compliance/VAT handling.

I've attached our RFP that outlines expected consumption patterns and procurement timelines. Can you confirm whether Redwood can support: (a) a two-tier discount corridor with volume smoothing, and (b) a reseller rebate expressed as a percentage of net revenue (we prefer 15% EMEA, 10% APAC)?

We can get procurement on a call early next week if you send a short MAP (mutual action plan) and a draft PO.

Thanks,
Liam
Liam O'Connor
CFO, Clearwater Health

Hi Liam — thanks for the RFP and the clear asks.

Short answers up front: yes on a two-tier corridor with smoothing, and yes we can operationalize a reseller rebate path — we typically handle that as (1) a distributor/reseller crediting workflow tied to invoicing or (2) when required, pass-through via marketplace private offer metadata (depends on marketplace constraints).

What I'd propose as an initial commercial construct: 

- Year 1 corridor: 0–$1.5M = 30% off list; $1.5M+ = 42% off list (blended target ~40% at your forecast).
- Volume smoothing: month-to-month smoothing up to +/-30% on consumption while preserving corridor eligibility (explicit lookback window and roll-forward).
- Channel rebate: 15% of net revenue to distributor in EMEA, 10% in APAC; credited quarterly against distributor invoices (we'll need distributor tax IDs and invoicing routing).

If that sounds directionally okay I can (a) send a short MAP and proposed PO draft, (b) loop in Jordan for ops (invoicing/marketplace path) and Ben for channel commissioning / commissioning playbook.

Proposed next steps:
1) Confirm region(s) and target pilot month.
2) Share distributor contacts + VAT handling notes.
3) Quick call Wednesday or Thursday to review the MAP.

I've attached a high-level pricing summary to illustrate the corridor math.

Best,
Naomi Feldman

Naomi / Ben — thanks for the heads up. Operational notes / recommendations: 

1) Invoicing path: prefer to push the deal through Marketplace Private Offer (MPO) when possible to keep billing consistent and avoid direct invoicing complexity. However, MPOs are limited in how much pass-through metadata they expose for distributor credits.

2) Practical approach we use: ingest MPO for the customer (keeps committed pricing), and run a separate distributor-crediting workflow where we issue quarterly credit memos to the distributor (credit percentage applied to Redwood's net revenue for the quarter). We'll need: distributor legal name, VAT/Tax ID, invoice recipient and email, and a signed distributor participation agreement. This avoids double taxation when credits are off-invoice.

3) EU VAT: require the distributor VAT ID and a short attestation. For EMEA rebate tax treatment, credits must be issued to the distributor invoice, not the end customer, to avoid pass-through VAT.

4) Timing & MAP: I can draft the MAP and ops checklist; suggest the MAP include a 2-week onboarding window for distributor setup (legal + tax).

Related links: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/4431 | draft MAP: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1a2b3c-clearwater-map

If you want, I can also propose two concrete invoicing flows (MPO + credit memos) vs direct invoicing with reseller pass-through. Ben — will the partner playbook need edits for the MPO case?

— Jordan
Jordan Blake
Head of Channel Operations | Redwood Inference
